title: Lottie Helps Lumina's Light
markdown:
The river sang a soft sleepy song. Lottie the little otter loved its tune. Her soft brown fur sparkled in the warm sun. Her bright eyes twinkled as she played in the water with her friend, Bean the bear cub. Bean had a soft warm voice and big furry ears. He was always happy to play. The sunbeams were like warm golden honey on the riverbank. It was a peaceful happy place.

Then Lottie saw Lumina the ladybug. Lumina’s little lantern sat on her back. It shone with a soft warm light. But Lumina looked a little worried. Her feelers drooped. “Hello, Lottie. Hello, Bean,” Lumina whispered. Her voice was like tiny bells. “I must go home. The dew is coming. My lantern light will get sleepy.”

Lottie felt a little wobble in her tummy. What if they could not help Lumina? What if her light got too sleepy?

“We will help you, Lumina,” rumbled Bean. His voice was like a soft song. Lottie nodded. The wobble felt a little bit smaller. “Yes. We will take you home.” Lumina’s home was in the quiet woods. It was not as bright as their river home. So Lumina sat on Lottie’s paw. Lottie and Bean walked together. They left the happy river. They went into the soft quiet woods.

The woods were pretty. Tall trees reached up like gentle giants. The ground was soft green moss, like a cozy carpet. But it was not as bright as home. The wobble tried to wiggle back. “Are we going the right way, Bean?” she whispered.

Suddenly, leaves rustled softly. Swish, swish, swish. Lottie froze. Her heart thumped like a tiny drum. A little shiver went down her back. Then she remembered. It was just the wind. The wind played with the leaves. It made them whisper secrets. Bean nudged her gently with his warm paw. “It is okay, Lottie.” His voice was like a soft sigh. Lottie took a deep breath, like the river breathing. She let the wobble float away like a little leaf.

Soon, through the green trees, they saw a big oak tree. Its branches reached out like wide arms. And there, at the tree, were Lumina’s family. They chirped happy sounds. Their little lanterns twinkled hello. Lumina was home. She was safe with her family. Her lantern shone bright and happy.

Lottie wanted to make sure it stayed bright for Lumina’s walk to her cozy nest. Lottie looked at her special pebble. It was smooth and cool. It had colours like tiny rainbows inside. She loved her pebble. It was her favourite. She kept it safe from the river.

Lottie held her pebble. It felt so good in her paw. She could smell the river on it. But Lumina needed help. Lottie took a tiny breath. She felt a little bit empty where the pebble used to be. “Here, Lumina,” Lottie said softly. “This pebble is lucky. It will help your lantern stay bright.”

Lottie and Bean waved goodbye to Lumina and her family. They walked back home. The woods felt friendly now. They were not a place for wobbles. Lottie felt a warm glow inside her. The happy feeling of helping a friend.

They reached their river home. The moon was a shy pearl in the sky. Silver light danced on the water. Tiny stars began to twinkle like diamond sprinkles on a soft blanket. Lottie felt brave. She felt happy. Her heart was full. The little wobbles felt very, very small now, like tiny whispers in the big quiet night. Bean gave a happy rumble. Lottie snuggled close to Bean. She felt safe and warm. She watched the stars drift by.

Lottie’s eyelids felt heavy. It was time to rest. The river sang its sleepy song. Lottie and Bean, safe and sound, closed their eyes. Soon they drifted off to sleep. They dreamed sweet dreams.
characters: Lottie (a little otter), Bean (a bear cub)
